archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose rushing value comes from breaking the pocket and scrambling rather than from called runs, paired with a passing game built on the intermediate middle of the field.

report.headline: Accuracy is back, the legs still carry him, but third downs stall the offense.
report.take:
Daniels arrived as a rookie who did everything: 0.204 EPA per play (9th) and 891 rushing yards (2nd) in 2024. Then 2025 came apart over seven games, with a -2.7 CPOE and 0.029 EPA per play. This season sits between those two. The accuracy has come back: his CPOE is 3.81, 11th of 55 and 6.5 points better than last year, and his bad-throw rate fell from 13.8% to 12.1%. The efficiency has not fully followed. His 0.015 passing EPA per dropback ranks 26th. It is above the league's -0.027, but it is nowhere near the rookie version. He still leads all quarterbacks in rushing yards, with 41.9 a game.

The passing value comes from one area. On throws of 10-19 air yards he is at 0.564 EPA per attempt with a 17.6 CPOE, and those 46 attempts account for most of what the passing game produces. Throws over the middle (0.313 EPA) work for the same reason. Antonio Williams has been the main beneficiary at 0.544 EPA per target, while Okonkwo and Rachaad White have lost value on their targets. The rushing works the same way. His 33 scrambles have gained 333 yards at 0.544 EPA each, with 13 first downs. His 10 designed runs have gone nowhere: 0.6 yards per carry, half of them stuffed. The legs pay off when the play breaks down, not when the run is called.

The averages hide two weak spots. The first is third down: -0.264 EPA, a 28.2% conversion rate, 7.5 yards to go on average, and 9 of his 20 sacks. The offense keeps getting behind schedule, and he has not been able to get it out. The second is game state. In one-score games he is at -0.063 EPA per play and has taken 17 sacks, while his best passing (0.218 EPA, 15.0 CPOE) has come trailing by nine or more. The sack rate (7.5%, 30th) looks like the old problem, but his pressure-to-sack rate of 32.1% is the best of his career, after 41.2% and 43.9% the last two years. Those sacks come from extending plays, and the scrambles more than pay for them.

The recent shape has shifted. Over the last three games he is throwing more, at 270.7 yards a game and 7.88 yards per attempt. He is running less: 26.4 rushing yards a game over his last five, against 41.9 for the season. His per-dropback EPA hasn't moved. Washington has won three of five behind a version of him that leans more on his arm. Arizona's pass defense, worst in the league, is a good place for that version to pay off.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for everything
strengths.body: When the pocket breaks down he turns it into yardage and first downs. That is his career-long identity, and it has held through a down 2025. These scrambles are the reason the sack rate is a price worth paying. Called runs add nothing, so the value depends on the play breaking down, which it reliably does.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy has returned
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards drive the passing game, with completion rates far above expectation. Overall CPOE has rebounded sharply from 2025 and is back near his rookie level. That points to a real fix rather than a hot streak, though 46 attempts is still a modest sample to carry an entire passing profile.

strengths.title: Ball security
strengths.body: Two interceptions on 248 attempts puts his INT rate well under the league average. Both came in one game at New York. His turnover-worthy plays are few. His aggressiveness is about the same as last year, so this is not coming from simply refusing to throw into windows.

concerns.title: Third downs are a dead zone
concerns.body: On third down his passing goes negative, conversions are rare, and nearly half his sacks come there. Long distances to go play a part, because the offense is often behind schedule. But this is where a top quarterback is supposed to bail out a mediocre offense, and he isn't yet. Until it improves, drives will stall and his touchdown volume will stay capped.

concerns.title: Deep ball isn't landing
concerns.body: Only a third of his 20+ yard throws are complete, and the CPOE there is below expectation, so the shots generate little beyond the occasional big gain. Screens and throws behind the line have been actively harmful, costing more EPA than any other depth. Both cut into the efficiency his intermediate game creates.

concerns.title: Rushing volume is fading
concerns.body: Over his last five games he is running far less than his season rate. Called runs have been abandoned for good reason, since they barely gain anything. If the scramble volume follows, his main edge over other passers shrinks. Fantasy managers should treat the 32-point game against New York as the ceiling, not the norm.

trend.note: His per-dropback efficiency has held flat over the last three and five games while the mix has shifted: more passing yards (270.7 a game over the last three), fewer rushing yards. The overall output looks much the same; how he gets it has changed.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense in football, but a low total caps volume
nextGame.body:
Arizona has the league's worst pass defense by EPA. It is near the bottom against short throws, deep throws and explosive plays, and it gives up the most fantasy points and touchdowns to quarterbacks. That fits Daniels well. His intermediate and middle-of-field game should find open windows, and a pass rush ranked mid-pack in sack rate and 24th in hit rate shouldn't force many of the breakdowns that cost him sacks. Arizona's run defense is solid (10th in rush EPA allowed), but his called runs weren't producing anyway, and scrambles don't depend on run fits. The one complication is the number: Washington -7.5 with a 40.5 total suggests a controlled, run-heavier script. His team has had a lead of nine or more on just one of his plays all season, so a comfortable lead would be new territory, and his volume could shrink in the second half.

Availability leans Washington's way. Arizona's starting quarterback, Carson Beck, was listed out with back spasms as of the latest report. A backup-led Cardinals offense, already 23rd in EPA, makes a Washington lead more likely and the game slower. Defensive tackle Zachary Carter is on IR, which thins their interior rush. On Washington's side, Laremy Tunsil remains on IR and isn't expected back this season. He hasn't played all year, so the protection Daniels has been working behind is the one he'll have, and no new loss touches him.

keyMatchups.title: Intermediate game vs a leaky secondary
keyMatchups.body: His best area is the 10-19 yard range, and Arizona allows big EPA at every depth. Its explosive pass rate allowed is among the league's worst. This is the matchup where his completion-over-expected edge should turn into yards.

keyMatchups.title: Okonkwo's chance to matter
keyMatchups.body: Arizona lets top tight ends score well above their usual output. Okonkwo has drawn plenty of targets but has been a negative-EPA option. If he converts here, it opens the middle further for Williams and Diggs.

keyMatchups.title: Game script against a backup QB
keyMatchups.body: With Beck out and the Book making Washington a heavy favorite at a low total, Washington should lead. A lead means fewer dropbacks late, and his scramble and rushing chances could come early rather than all game.

nextGame.watch: Whether Washington keeps throwing once it's ahead or turns the game over to the run, since that decides whether this matchup delivers big passing numbers or just a comfortable win.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy rebound looks real. It shows in his CPOE, his bad-throw rate and a cleaner pressure-to-sack rate than in either previous season, so expect his completion rate and yards per attempt to stay above league average. The intermediate efficiency will probably come down some from 0.564 EPA per attempt on 46 throws, and the deep game has room to improve, so his passing efficiency should hold roughly where it is. A projection of 225 to 270 passing yards a game reflects the heavier passing role of recent weeks. The main lever for improvement is third down: if the conversion rate climbs even modestly, his touchdown total picks up.

The rushing is the bigger question. Scrambles carry his whole rushing profile, and his recent rushing yards have fallen well under his season rate, so 28 to 42 rushing yards a game is a fairer projection than his season average. That puts him around 16 to 21 PPR points a game, enough to stay a top-ten fantasy quarterback but without the rookie-year ceiling.
swingFactors: Deep-ball completions to Diggs and Williams

confidence.note: Eight games with missed time; the accuracy rebound is supported, but key splits rest on small samples.
